en.title: The Duskbloods Network Test Outperforms Elden Ring in Applications
en.summary: A recent network test for an upcoming Switch 2 exclusive, The Duskbloods, has seen an overwhelming number of applications, surpassing even the highly anticipated Elden Ring network test. This surge in interest highlights the growing anticipation for new hardware and FromSoftware's continued appeal.
en.body:
The anticipation for next-generation gaming hardware is palpable, and the early indicators for the upcoming **Switch 2** are looking exceptionally strong. Developer FromSoftware, renowned for its brutally challenging yet deeply rewarding titles like the **Dark Souls** series and **Elden Ring**, recently concluded a closed network test for its new game, **The Duskbloods**. In a surprising turn of events that underscores the burgeoning excitement for the new console, this test attracted more player applications than the network test for the immensely popular **Elden Ring: Shadow of the Erdtree** expansion, despite **The Duskbloods** being exclusive to a single, unreleased platform.

This remarkable turnout suggests that the allure of FromSoftware's design philosophy, coupled with the promise of new hardware capabilities, is a potent combination. While **Elden Ring**'s network test was available across multiple platforms and for a game already a massive success, **The Duskbloods** test was limited to the **Switch 2**, a device not yet widely available. This exclusivity did not deter players; instead, it seems to have fueled the desire to be among the first to experience what FromSoftware has in store, potentially setting a new benchmark for early hardware engagement.

## A New Challenger Appears

FromSoftware has consistently delivered critically acclaimed titles that define genres and push the boundaries of player engagement. Their games are known for intricate world-building, deep lore, and demanding combat that rewards patience and skill. The success of **Elden Ring**, which sold over 23 million units as of March 2024, cemented their status as one of the most influential developers in the industry. The fact that a network test for a new IP, exclusive to a yet-to-be-released console, could generate more interest than the test for a major expansion of their most successful game speaks volumes about the trust and excitement players have for the studio's future endeavors.

This phenomenon is particularly noteworthy given the **Switch 2**'s positioning. While official details remain scarce, the gaming community is abuzz with speculation about its potential power and features. The overwhelming response to **The Duskbloods** network test could be interpreted as a strong signal of developer confidence in the new hardware, suggesting that it will offer a compelling platform for ambitious titles. It also indicates that players are willing to invest in new ecosystems if the content promises to be as compelling as the established hits.

## Fan Frenzy and Future Implications

The gaming community is understandably thrilled by these early numbers. For fans of FromSoftware, this is a clear sign that their next great adventure is on the horizon and that the **Switch 2** might be a platform worth investing in. The high application numbers suggest a significant portion of the player base is eager to dive into challenging gameplay and explore new worlds, regardless of platform. This enthusiasm translates into high expectations for **The Duskbloods** and potentially for the **Switch 2** itself. The success of this network test could influence platform holder strategies and developer commitments moving forward, highlighting the power of exclusive, high-profile content.

## What's Next

While specific release dates for **The Duskbloods** and the **Switch 2** have not yet been announced, this network test performance serves as a powerful indicator of market interest. Players should keep an eye on official announcements from Nintendo and FromSoftware for further details on both the game and the new console. The gaming world will be watching closely to see if this initial surge in interest translates into long-term success for both.
